next_round_constraints: Keep SEIRS as the primary structure family; deprioritize SEIR unless paired with a compelling observation/lag change.
Focus on delayed_I observation mapping; treat delay as a discrete hyperparameter and prioritize testing around 2 weeks (include 2 as anchor; optionally bracket with 1 and 3 only if budget allows).
Avoid adding hospitalization compartment mappings (H or I+H) unless accompanied by a clear simplification elsewhere (e.g., fewer free parameters) to control complexity and improve identifiability.
Maintain fractional dynamics as default for this series; only test non-fractional variants if they keep the same observation map and delay to isolate the effect of fractional vs non-fractional.
observed_failure_modes: Delay sensitivity: delayed_I with 1-week delay shows strong degradation relative to 2-week delay, suggesting the observation lag is critical and mis-specification causes large errors.

Structure mismatch for hospitalization target: SEIHR with H or I+H observation maps underperforms, indicating the added H compartment/observation mapping may be misaligned with the rate dynamics or introduces unnecessary degrees of freedom for this series.
Over/under-flexibility tradeoff: SEIR (no S-loss/waning) performs worse than SEIRS, implying reinfection/waning (or equivalent flexibility) is needed to capture the high-peak, high-scale dynamics.

Stability concerns across rolling splits for non-best candidates: several alternatives show higher rolling variability, consistent with parameter non-identifiability or sensitivity to initialization when the template is not well matched.
